figure: n/a — prose page (no figure on this page); reviewed because it supplies the arithmetic that Figure 15.1 (PDF 248) rests on
issue: The attention-FLOP substitution is arithmetically false by two orders of magnitude, and the error inverts the book's own conclusion about which term dominates prefill. The text states: "the per-layer cost is ~ 4 · L² · d_model, where d_model = 8,192. That is 4 × 9,200² × 8,192 = 2.2 × 10¹⁶ FLOPs — the quadratic attention term that grows dominant at long context." The left-hand side of that substitution evaluates to 4 × 84,640,000 × 8,192 = 2.77 × 10¹² FLOPs per layer, not 2.2 × 10¹⁶. Multiplying by the 80 layers named in the preceding clause ("Across 80 layers that is ...") gives 2.22 × 10¹⁴ FLOPs — i.e. the printed exponent should be 10¹⁴, not 10¹⁶. The printed 2.2 × 10¹⁶ is exactly what one obtains with L = 92,000 rather than 9,200, which suggests a dropped factor of ten in L.
evidence: Recomputed: 4 × 9,200² × 8,192 = 2.773e12 (per layer); × 80 layers = 2.218e14. Cross-check against the book's own dense-matmul estimate on the same page: 2P/token with P = 70e9 gives 1.4e11 FLOP/token; over the canonical 9,200-token prompt that is 1.29e15 FLOP. So at the canonical context, attention (2.2e14, or 1.1e14 if the causal half is taken) is roughly 8–17% of the prefill cost, NOT the dominant term. The printed 2.2e16 would make attention ~17× the dense-matmul term and would be the only thing that makes the clause "grows dominant at long context" true at 9,200 tokens. The error therefore propagates into the reader's mental model of the prefill/decode cost split and into the roofline reasoning that Figure 15.1 illustrates.
acceptance_test: The printed substitution must evaluate to the printed result. Correct to "4 × 9,200² × 8,192 ≈ 2.8 × 10¹² FLOPs per layer; across 80 layers ≈ 2.2 × 10¹⁴ FLOPs", and the sentence must then say that attention is a minority term at the canonical 9,200-token context and becomes dominant only at substantially longer contexts (state the crossover, e.g. the L at which 4·L²·d·80 exceeds 1.4e11·L). Separately, state explicitly whether the 4·L²·d convention is causal or dense: causal attention is 2·L²·d per layer, so the factor of two must be declared and used consistently wherever attention FLOPs are compared with the 2P/token dense term.

figure: Figure 15.1 — FlashAttention: the same math, far less HBM traffic
issue: In the BEFORE panel, the red annotation reads "O(L²) HBM traffic: every query re-reads the K/V row-block". The colon attributes the O(L²) traffic to K/V row-block re-reads — but K/V row-block reads from HBM are O(L²) in BOTH the naive and FlashAttention implementations (each query tile still needs all K/V). The quantity that actually drops is the materialized L×L intermediate, which the AFTER panel mentions only as "no L×L intermediate at HBM" with no complexity label. Juxtaposing an "O(L²)" label on the left against no complexity label on the right invites the reader to infer that FlashAttention changes the asymptotic HBM-traffic class — precisely the "quadratic-to-linear swap" misconception that the book's own prose on PDF 247 explicitly warns against ("the precise I/O complexity is more nuanced than a clean quadratic-to-linear swap").
evidence: Fig 15.1 BEFORE panel: "O(L²) HBM traffic: every query re-reads the K/V row-block". AFTER panel: "K/V reused per tile — no single global K/V pass; no L×L intermediate at HBM" (no big-O label). Prose on PDF 247 / printed 227: "the precise I/O complexity is more nuanced than a clean quadratic-to-linear swap, but the materialized-intermediate traffic is what drops". The caption scopes the "read once" claim but does not scope the O(L²) label.
acceptance_test: Relabel the BEFORE annotation so the O(L²) attaches to the intermediate (e.g., "O(L²) intermediate traffic: the L×L scores matrix is written to HBM and re-read"), and/or add a matching qualifier to the AFTER panel (e.g., "K/V reads still O(L²) — fewer round-trips, not sub-quadratic"). Rebuild and confirm a reader cannot infer an asymptotic-class change from the figure alone, consistent with the PDF 247 prose.

figure: FIGURE 15.1 'FlashAttention: the same math, far less HBM traffic', AFTER panel
issue: The AFTER panel draws exactly two arrows between the on-chip box and the HBM box (one up, one down), which reads as 'read K/V once, write once' — i.e. a single global K/V pass. The caption explicitly disclaims that reading: "the tile-level on-chip reuse is per-tile: it is not a guarantee that every K/V element is read exactly once globally across all query blocks (the exact number of K/V re-reads depends on the tile scheduling, sequence length, and SRAM size)". The in-panel note ('KV reused per tile — no single global K/V pass') mitigates but does not resolve the conflict, because the drawn arrow count is the strongest visual signal and it encodes exactly the claim the caption retracts.
evidence: Rendered page: BEFORE panel shows a fan of ~7 red arrows; AFTER panel shows 2 green arrows. The caption's scope note is the only textual guard against reading the 2 arrows as 'one global read'. A reader scanning the figure will take the arrow count as the traffic story.
acceptance_test: Label the AFTER arrows with what they represent (e.g. 'read K/V block per tile' and 'write O only') and add an in-panel note that the number of K/V re-reads equals the number of query tiles, or replace the arrow count with a per-tile loop glyph so the figure cannot be read as a single global pass. The figure must not, by arrow count alone, assert a global single-read.

issue: The headline claims 'far less HBM traffic' (a byte quantity) while the figure's own bottom line and the caption both claim 'fewer HBM round-trips' (a count). That is a rate, not a byte count.' The headline therefore uses the weaker claim's units for the stronger claim's benefit.
evidence: Rendered page: headline 'FlashAttention: the same math, far less HBM traffic'; in-panel green line 'the gain is fewer HBM round-trips, not cheaper attention'; caption 'the gain is fewer HBM round-trips, not a change to the attention mathematics'.
acceptance_test: Change the headline to 'far fewer HBM round-trips' (or state the traffic reduction explicitly, e.g. 'O(L²) → O(L) HBM traffic for the intermediate'), so that the headline, the in-panel line, and the caption use one unit.

figure: FIGURE 15.1, BEFORE panel, HBM box label

acceptance_test: Label the BEFORE panel's HBM box to include the intermediate (e.g. 'Q/K/V + O(L²) intermediate') and, if space permits, draw the intermediate as a distinct hatched region so the reader sees what the naive path materializes.
